name: GUM (JCGM 100:2008) clause 7: reporting uncertainty
citation: JCGM 100:2008. Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM), clause 7 'Reporting uncertainty' (7.1 general guidance, 7.2 specific guidance). Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology, BIPM, 2008; text read on 2026-11-23 at https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf. The clause has no numbered checklist: items are numbered 1-18 here, and each topic starts with the subclause (and list letter) it paraphrases. Where 7.2.1 (standard uncertainty) and 7.2.3 (expanded uncertainty) ask the same, one item carries the 7.2.1 label.

items.topic: 7.1.2 Referenced procedures match what was done
items.question: Where the method or uncertainty evaluation is given by reference to published documents, are those current and do they match the procedure actually used?

items.topic: 7.1.4a How result and uncertainty were computed
items.question: Is it clear how the result and its uncertainty were calculated from the observations and the input data?

items.topic: 7.1.4b Every uncertainty component and its evaluation
items.question: Are all uncertainty components listed, each with how it was evaluated (Type A from repeated observations or Type B otherwise)?

items.topic: 7.1.4c Analysis steps a reader can repeat
items.question: Is the data analysis laid out so each important step can be followed and the reported result recomputed independently?
Are all corrections and constants used in the analysis given, with where each comes from?
Is the measurand (the quantity intended to be measured) defined completely, including the conditions it refers to?

items.topic: 7.2.1b Estimate with its uncertainty and units
items.question: Wherever a result is reported, is the estimate given with its combined standard or expanded uncertainty, both with units?
Where it helps the reader (and the estimate is not zero), is the relative uncertainty also given?
Where useful to users, are the effective degrees of freedom given, and the Type A and Type B combined parts with theirs?

items.topic: 7.2.2 Unambiguous way of writing the result
items.question: Is it unambiguous which uncertainty a written result carries (e.g. a value plus-minus a standard uncertainty is not read as an interval)?
For an expanded uncertainty, is the coverage factor k stated (ideally with the combined standard uncertainty)?

items.topic: 7.2.3e Level of confidence and its basis
items.question: For an expanded uncertainty, is the approximate level of confidence of the interval given, and how it was determined (e.g. a t distribution)?
If several measurands come from the same measurement, are their covariances or correlation coefficients reported?
Are uncertainties quoted to about two significant digits and estimates rounded consistently with their uncertainty?
Is each input estimate given with its standard uncertainty and a description of how both were obtained (an uncertainty budget)?
If input estimates are correlated, are their covariances or correlation coefficients given, with the method used to obtain them?

items.topic: 7.2.7c Degrees of freedom of each input
items.question: Are the degrees of freedom of each input's standard uncertainty given, with how they were obtained?
Is the measurement model relating the measurand to its inputs given (or the program computing it cited), with any experimentally found sensitivity coefficients?
